races.name: Firbolg

traits.name: Powerful Build
traits.description: The firbolg counts as one size larger when determining its carrying capacity and the weight it can push, drag, or lift.

traits.name: Speech of Beast and Leaf
traits.description: The firbolg can communicate in a limited way with Beasts and Plants. These creatures understand the meaning of the firbolg's words, though the firbolg has no ability to understand their languages. In addition, the firbolg has advantage on Charisma checks it makes to influence a Beast or Plant.

races.description: Firbolgs are forest-dwelling Humanoids native to the Greying Wild lands of Wildemount. They are on the tall side of Medium, and their bodies are covered with thick fur ranging in color from tones of brown and ruddy red to cool gray and blue, and occasionally in hues of pink or green.

Powerful Build.notes: Counts as one size larger when determining carrying capacity and weight it can push, drag, or lift.

Speech of Beast and Leaf.notes: Can communicate in a limited way with Beasts and Plants; they understand the firbolg's words but the firbolg cannot understand their languages. Advantage on Charisma checks to influence a Beast or Plant.

magic_items.name: Emerald Eye
magic_items.description: The amulet is the Emerald Eye- the goal of this race. The amulet, which is made of gold and emeralds, is worth 500 gp- though no one in Jig ow will buy it, since it must be returned the town elders once the contest is completed.

magic_items.name: Jewel of Three Prayers
magic_items.description:
The jewel of Three Prayers is a Vestige of Divergence (see the "Vestiges of Divergence" sidebar). In ancient times, Alyxian the Apotheon bore this amulet as a symbol of his covenant with three Prime Deities: Sehanine the Moon Weaver, Avandra the Change Bringer, and Corellon the Arch Heart. When the jewel is found, only Sehanine's power thrums within its dormant heart. The power of the other two deities waits to be reawakened by a hero- or heroes- who can follow in Alyxian's footsteps.

Dormant State. In this state, the jewel of Three Prayers is a glittering golden disk attached to a fine golden chain. The chain magically resizes to function as a necklace for the creature that wears it.
In its Dormant State, the jewel has the following properties:
• You gain a +l bonus to AC while wearing the jewel.
• While wearing or holding the jewel, you can use an action to cause it to shed bright light in a 15-foot radius and dim light for an additional 15 feet. The light lasts until you extinguish it (no action required).
• The jewel has 3 charges and regains all its expended charges daily at dawn. While holding the jewel, you can expend 1 charge from it to cast the invisibility spell.

Awakened State. In this state, the jewel has received the blessing of Avandra the Change Bringer. Three delicate spires unfurl from the jewel's center, like the buds of flowers opening in the spring. Three lapis lazuli stones rest like dewdrops on these spires.
The following benefits of the jewel improve:
The bonus that the jewel confers to your AC increases to +2.
• Its number of charges increases to 5.
The jewel gains the following additional properties, which you can use while wearing or holding it:
• You can expend 1 of the jewel's charges (no action required) to end one of the following conditions on yourself: grappled, paralyzed, or restrained.
• When another creature you can see within 60 feet of you fails a saving throw, you can expend 1 of the jewel's charges as a reaction to enable that creature to reroll the saving throw, potentially turning a failure into a success. The creature must use the new roll.

Exalted State. In this state, the jewel has received the blessing of Corellon the Arch Heart. A gleaming emerald surrounded by a halo of gold appears on the jewel.
The following benefits of the jewel improve:
• The bonus that the jewel confers to your AC increases to +3.
• Its number of charges increases to 7.
The jewel gains the following additional properties, which you can use while wearing or holding it:
• You gain the ability to breathe water, and you gain a swimming speed equal to your walking speed.
• Each of your allies within 30 feet of you gains the ability to breathe water and gains a swimming speed equal to its walking speed.
• As a bonus action, you can expend 1 of the jewel's charges to target yourself or one willing creature you can see within 15 feet of yourself. The target teleports to an unoccupied space of your choice within 15 feet of yourself, along with any equipment the target is wearing or carrying. The target appears in a flash of golden radiance, and each creature of your choice within 5 feet of the target's new location must make a DC 18 Constitution saving throw. On a failed save, the creature takes 4d10 radiant damage and is blinded until the start of your next turn. On a successful save, the creature takes half as much damage and isn't blinded.

magic_items.name: +1 dagger
magic_items.description: A +1 dagger embedded in the hide of the udaak. The dagger is inscribed with the name of its owner, Kierchaly Wastewalker.

magic_items.name: Spell Scroll of Bestow Curse
magic_items.description: A folded-up spell scroll of bestow curse.

magic_items.name: Mote of Possibility
magic_items.description: A magical Mote of Possibility, which manifests as a flash of silver light as he touches each character's forehead in turn. A character who fails a saving throw or misses on an attack roll can use a reaction to expend their Mote of Possibility, allowing them to reroll the d20. The character must use the new roll. A Mote of Possibility vanishes from a character after 24 hours or when it is expended.

magic_items.name: Sword of Vengeance
magic_items.description: A character who searches the bodies finds an onyx-hilted longsword that has become a sword of vengeance haunted by the spirit of its former wielder.

magic_items.name: driftglobe (cracked)
magic_items.description: In its damaged state, the driftglobe can be used only to cast the light spell.

magic_items.name: Nolzur's Marvelous Pigments
magic_items.description: A set of Nolzur's marvelous pigments.

magic_items.name: Magically Preserved Wine
magic_items.description: Olara has three bottles of this delicious, pre-Divergence vintage in stock and asks 50 gp per bottle. An Ank'Hareli sommelier will pay up to 1,000 gp for a bottle of this rare vintage.

magic_items.name: Potions of Healing
magic_items.description: Olara has five of potions of healing in stock and sells them for 50 gp each.

magic_items.name: Potions of Heroism
magic_items.description: Olara has two potions of heroism in stock and sells them for 300 gp each.

magic_items.name: Ruidium Shield
magic_items.description:
Tendrils of ruidium extend across the metal surface of this shield. While this shield is on your person, you gain the following benefits:
• You have resistance to psychic damage.
• You can breathe water.
• You gain a swimming speed equal to your walking speed.

Psychic Reflection. When you take psychic damage while holding the shield, you can use your reaction to choose another creature you can see within 30 feet of you. That creature takes the psychic damage you would have taken.

Ruidium Corruption. When you use the shield's Psychic Reflection property, you must make a DC 20 Charisma saving throw. On a failed save, you gain 1 level of exhaustion. If you are not already suffering from ruidium corruption, you become corrupted when you fail this save.

If Ruidium Is Destroyed. If the Apotheon is killed or redeemed, all the ruidium in Exandria is destroyed instantly, and a ruidium shield becomes a +2 shield.

magic_items.name: Ruidium Shortsword
magic_items.description: A shortsword with veins of ruidium. See appendix B for full description.

magic_items.name: ruidium greataxe
magic_items.description: Embedded in the death embrace's bell is a ruidium greataxe (see appendix B), the so-called Key to the Netherdeep that the Allegiance of Allsight and the Consortium of the Vermilion Dream are after (see chapter 4).

magic_items.name: sentinel shield
magic_items.description: A sentinel shield and a frost brand longsword.

magic_items.name: frost brand longsword
magic_items.description: A sentinel shield and a frost brand longsword.

magic_items.name: Fragment of Pity
magic_items.description:
The mote of light above the pedestal is the Fragment of Pity (see "Fragments of Suffering" earlier in the chapter). When a character touches the mote, it disappears and becomes part of the character's soul. When this happens, all the characters receive a fleeting vision (see the Apotheon Lore table earlier in the chapter).
The character who is carrying the Fragment of Pity gains the following benefit and drawback, and is aware of both:
Benefit. Each time you spend a Hit Die to regain hit points, you regain additional hit points equal to your proficiency bonus.
Drawback. You have disadvantage on death saving throws.

magic_items.name: Ruidium Greatsword
magic_items.description: A ruidium greatsword (described in appendix B)

magic_items.name: Spear (replica of Alyxian's spear)
magic_items.description: The spear sticking out of the pile of bones is a replica of Alyxian's spear. It shows no signs of rust, decay, or ruidium corruption, unlike the other weapons found throughout the chamber. It is imbued with the properties of a weapon of warning.

magic_items.name: Fragment of Deception
magic_items.description: When a character touches the mote of light in the Moon Weaver's cupped hands, it disappears and becomes part of the character's soul. When this happens, all the characters receive a fleeting vision (see the Apotheon Lore table earlier in the chapter). The character who is carrying the Fragment of Deception gains the following benefit and drawback, and is aware of both: Benefit. When you take damage, you can use your reaction to turn invisible and teleport up to 60 feet to an unoccupied space you can see. You remain invisible until the start of your next turn or until you make a damage roll or cast a spell. Drawback. You have disadvantage on Wisdom checks.

magic_items.name: Irvan's Prosthetic Arm
magic_items.description: During a misadventure that unfolded while the rivals were apart from the characters, Irvan Wastewalker lost an arm and gained an arcane prosthetic. This magic item functions for no one else.

magic_items.name: Breathing Bubble
magic_items.description:
This translucent, bubble-like sphere has a slightly tacky outer surface. The bubble contains 1 hour of breathable air. The bubble regains all its expended air daily at dawn.
You gain the item's benefits by wearing it over your head like a helmet. When it's not being worn, the breathing bubble retains its bubble shape.

magic_items.name: Earring of Message
magic_items.description: The blue crystal of this earring is wrapped with delicate copper wire. The earring has 5 charges. While wearing it, you can use an action to expend 1 charge and cast the message spell. The earring regains 1d4 + 1 expended charges daily at dawn.

magic_items.name: Medal of Muscle
magic_items.description: You can squeeze this medal tightly in the palm of your hand as an action. Doing so gives you advantage on Strength checks and Strength saving throws for 1 hour. Once this property has been used, it can't be used again, and the medal becomes nonmagical.

magic_items.name: Medal of the Conch
magic_items.description: When you use an action to rub this medal, you gain a swimming speed equal to your walking speed for 1 hour. Once this property has been used, it can't be used again, and the medal becomes nonmagical.

magic_items.name: Medal of the Horizonback
magic_items.description: When you would be hit by an attack, you can use your reaction to increase your AC by 5 until the start of your next turn, including against the triggering attack. You must be wearing the medal arid able to see the creature that made the triggering attack to use this property. Once this property has been used, it can't be used again, and the medal becomes nonmagical.

magic_items.name: Medal of the Maze
magic_items.description: When you use an action to trace the maze inscribed on this medal, you gain advantage on Wisdom checks and know the quickest route to the end of any nonmagical path or maze for 1 hour. Once this property has been used, it can't be used again, and the medal becomes nonmagical.

magic_items.name: Medal of the Meat Pie
magic_items.description:
You gain 2d4 + 2 temporary hit points when you use an action to press this medal to your mouth. Once this property has been used, it can't be used again, and the medal becomes nonmagical.
While magical, this medal is slightly warm to the touch (as if it's fresh from the oven) and smells faintly of baked pie crust.

magic_items.name: Medal of the Wetlands
magic_items.description: When you use an action to trace the edge of this medal, difficult terrain doesn't cost you extra movement for 1 hour. Once this property has been used, it can't be used again, and the medal becomes nonmagical.

magic_items.name: Medal of Wit
magic_items.description: You can press this medal to your temple as an action. Doing so gives you advantage on Intelligence checks and Intelligence saving throws for 1 hour. Once this property has been used, it can't be used again, and the medal becomes nonmagical.

magic_items.name: Ring of Red Fury
magic_items.description:
This ring has a crimson gemstone in its center. When you wear the ring, you can use a bonus action to activate it for 1 minute or until you are incapacitated: 
• You have advantage on Strength checks and Strength saving throws. 
• When you hit with an attack, you can add your proficiency bonus to the damage roll. 
• Difficult terrain doesn't cost you extra movement, and you are immune to the paralyzed and restrained conditions. 
You can't use this property of the ring again until you finish a long rest.

Ruidium Corruption. When you use the Ruidium Rage property of the ring, you must make a DC 20 Charisma saving throw. On a failed save, you gain 1 level of exhaustion. If you are not already suffering from ruidium corruption, you become corrupted when you fail this save.

If Ruidium Is Destroyed. If the Apotheon is killed or redeemed, all the ruidium in Exandria is destroyed instantly, and the ring of red fury becomes a ring of free action.

magic_items.name: Ruidium Armor
magic_items.type: Armor (Any Medium or Heavy Except Hide)
magic_items.description:
This magic armor has a dull, rusty color or has veins of ruidium running through it. While you wear this armor, you gain the following benefits:
• You have resistance to psychic damage.
• You can breathe water.
• You gain a swimming speed equal to your walking speed.

Ruidium Corruption. When you roll a 1 on a saving throw while wearing this armor, you must make a DC 15 Charisma saving throw. On a failed save, you gain 1 level of exhaustion. If you are not already suffering from ruidium corruption, you become corrupted when you fail this save.

If Ruidium Is Destroyed. If the Apotheon is killed or redeemed, all the ruidium in Exandria is destroyed instantly, and ruidium armor becomes +1 armor.

magic_items.name: Ruidium Weapon
magic_items.description:
This magic weapon has a dull, rusty color or has veins of ruidium running through it. While this weapon is on your person, you gain the following benefits:
• You can breathe water.
• You gain a swimming speed equal to your walking speed.

Ruidium Strike. A creature you hit with this weapon takes an extra 2d6 psychic damage.

Ruidium Corruption. When you roll a 1 on an attack roll made with this weapon, you must make a DC 20 Charisma saving throw. On a failed save, you gain 1 level of exhaustion. If you are not already suffering from ruidium corruption, you become corrupted when you fail this save.

If Ruidium Is Destroyed. If the Apotheon is killed or redeemed, all the ruidium in Exandria is destroyed instantly, and a ruidium weapon becomes a +2 weapon.

magic_items.name: Teleportation Tablet
magic_items.description:
This clay tablet is eight inches long, four inches wide, and half an inch thick. Inscribed on it is the sigil sequence for a permanent teleportation circle. A creature that studies the sequence for 10 minutes can make a DC 21 Intelligence (Arcana) check, learning the circle's destination on a success.

You can use an action to break the tablet in half, turning it to dust. If the tablet is broken while it is on the same plane of existence as the teleportation circle whose sigil sequence was engraved on it, a 10-foot-diameter teleportation circle of glowing blue light appears on the ground in an unoccupied space you choose within 30 feet of you. This teleportation circle has the characteristics of one created using the teleportation circle spell, except that it connects to the teleportation circle whose sigil sequence appears on the tablet.

The teleportation circle created by the tablet disappears at the end of your next turn.

features.name: Fey Ancestry
features.description: Verin has advantage on saving throws against being charmed, and magic can't put him to sleep.

features.name: Sunlight Sensitivity
features.description: While in sunlight, Verin has disadvantage on attack rolls, as well as on Wisdom (Perception) checks that rely on sight.

actions.name: Multiattack
actions.description: Verin makes three Glaive attacks.

actions.name: Glaive
actions.description: Melee Weapon Attack: +7 to hit, reach 10 ft., one target. Hit: 9 (1d10 + 4) slashing damage.

actions.name: Hand Crossbow
actions.description: Ranged Weapon Attack: +7 to hit, range 30/120 ft., one target. Hit: 5 (1d6 + 2) piercing damage plus 22 (4d10) poison damage.

actions.name: Spellcasting
actions.description: Verin casts one of the following spells, requiring no material components and using Charisma as the spellcasting ability (spell save DC 14): At will: dancing lights. 1/day each: darkness, faerie fire, levitate (self only).

reactions.name: Parry
reactions.description: Verin adds 3 to his AC against one melee attack that would hit him. To do so, he must see the attacker and be wielding a melee weapon.

features.name: Sunlight Sensitivity
features.description: While in sunlight, the gloomstalker has disadvantage on attack rolls, as well as on Wisdom (Perception) checks that rely on sight.

actions.name: Multiattack
actions.description: The gloomstalker makes one Bite attack and one Claw attack.

actions.name: Bite
actions.description: Melee Weapon Attack: +9 to hit, reach 5 ft., one creature. Hit: 15 (2d8 + 6) piercing damage plus 7 (2d6) necrotic damage.

actions.name: Claw
actions.description: Melee Weapon Attack: +9 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit: 13 (2d6 + 6) slashing damage plus 7 (2d6) necrotic damage.

actions.name: Snatch
actions.description: Melee Weapon Attack: +9 to hit, reach 5 ft., one Medium or smaller creature. Hit: 13 (2d6 + 6) slashing damage plus 7 (2d6) necrotic damage, and the target is grappled (escape DC 17). While grappled in this way, the target is restrained.

actions.name: Shriek (Recharge 6)
actions.description: The gloomstalker emits a terrible shriek. Each enemy within 60 feet of the gloomstalker that can hear it must succeed on a DC 13 Constitution saving throw or be paralyzed until the end of the enemy's next turn.

features.name: Shapechanger
features.description: The succubus/incubus can use its action to polymorph into a Small or Medium humanoid, or back into its true form. Without its wings, it loses its flying speed. Other statistics are the same in each form. Any equipment it is wearing or carrying isn't transformed. It reverts to its true form if it dies.

features.name: Telepathic Bond
features.description: The fiend ignores the range restriction on its telepathy when communicating with a creature it has charmed. The two don't even need to be on the same plane of existence.

actions.name: Claw (Fiend Form Only)
actions.description: Melee Weapon Attack: +5 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit: 6 (1d6+3) slashing damage.

actions.name: Charm
actions.description: One humanoid the fiend can see within 30 feet of it must succeed on a DC 15 Wisdom saving throw or be magically charmed for 1 day. The charmed target obeys the fiend's verbal or telepathic commands. If the target suffers any harm or receives a suicidal command, it can repeat the saving throw, ending the effect on a success. If the target successfully saves against the effect, or if the effect on it ends, the target is immune to this fiend's Charm for the next 24 hours. The fiend can have only one target charmed at a time. If it charms another, the effect on the previous target ends.

actions.name: Etherealness
actions.description: The fiend magically enters the Ethereal Plane from the Material Plane, or vice versa.

monsters.name: Ruidium Elephant

features.name: Trampling Charge
features.description: If the elephant moves at least 20 feet straight toward a creature and then hits it with a Gore attack on the same turn, that target must succeed on a DC 16 Strength saving throw or be knocked prone. If the target is prone, the elephant can make one Stomp attack against it as a bonus action.

actions.name: Gore
actions.description: Melee Weapon Attack: +10 to hit (with advantage if the target is a creature missing any hit points), reach 10 ft., one target. Hit: 25 (4d8 + 7) piercing damage plus 7 (2d6) psychic damage.

actions.name: Stomp
actions.description: Melee Weapon Attack: +10 to hit, reach 5 ft., one prone creature. Hit: 29 (4d10 + 7) bludgeoning damage plus 7 (2d6) psychic damage.

monsters.source: Call of the Netherdeep (page not determinable from text)

features.name: Keen Sight and Smell
features.description: The vulture has advantage on Wisdom (Perception) checks that rely on sight or smell.

features.name: Pack Tactics
features.description: The vulture has advantage on an attack roll against a creature if at least one of the vulture's allies is within 5 feet of the creature and the ally isn't incapacitated.

actions.name: Multiattack
actions.description: The vulture makes two attacks: one with its beak and one with its talons.

actions.name: Beak
actions.description: Melee Weapon Attack: +4 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit: 7 (2d4+2) piercing damage.

actions.name: Talons
actions.description: Melee Weapon Attack: +4 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit: 9 (2d6+2) slashing damage.

features.name: Abo/ethic Vessel
features.description: The spawn must obey its aboleth master.

features.name: Amphibious
features.description: The spawn can breathe air and water.

features.name: Water Dependency
features.description: The spawn takes 6 (1dl2) acid damage every 10 minutes it goes without being immersed in water.

actions.name: Multiattack
actions.description: The spawn makes one Spear attack, two Tentacle attacks, and one Psychic Lash attack.

actions.name: Spear
actions.description: Melee or Ranged Weapon Attack: +7 to hit, reach 5 ft. or range 20/60 ft., one target. Hit: 7 (1d6 + 4) piercing damage, or 8 (1d8 + 4) piercing damage when used with two hands to make a melee attack.

actions.name: Tentacle
actions.description: Melee Weapon Attack: +7 to hit, reach 10 ft., one creature. Hit: The target is grappled (escape DC 14) and takes 9 (2d8) psychic damage at the start of each of its turns until the grapple ends. The spawn has four tentacles, each of which can grapple one creature.

actions.name: Psychic Lash
actions.description: Ranged Spell Attack: +7 to hit, range 120 ft., one creature. Hit: 18 (4d8) psychic damage.

monsters.name: Death Embrace
monsters.senses: blindsight 60 ft. (blind beyond this radius), passive Perception 9

features.name: Petrifying Tendrils
features.description: Any creature that starts its turn in the death embrace's space must make a DC 16 Constitution saving throw. On a failed saving throw, the creature is restrained. A creature restrained in this way must repeat the saving throw at the end of its next turn, becoming petrified on a failed saving throw or ending the effect on a successful one. The petrified condition lasts until the effect is ended by a greater restoration spell or similar magic.

features.name: Reel
features.description: At the start of each of its turns, the death embrace can pull each creature it is grappling up to 20 feet toward it (no action required).

features.name: Water Breathing
features.description: The death embrace can breathe only underwater.

actions.name: Multiattack
actions.description: The death embrace makes two Tentacle attacks.

actions.name: Tentacle
actions.description: Melee Weapon Attack: +10 to hit, reach 60 ft., one target. Hit: 13 (2d6 + 6) piercing damage plus 11 (2d10) psychic damage. If the target is Large or smaller, it is also grappled (escape DC 16). The death embrace has six tentacles, each of which can grapple one target.

reactions.name: Body Shield
reactions.description: When the death embrace is hit by an attack, one creature the death embrace is grappling (chosen by the death embrace) takes the damage instead.

monsters.name: Sword Wraith Warrior
damage_resistances: bludgeoning, piercing, and slashing from nonmagical attacks
languages: the languages it knew in life

features.name: Unusual Nature
features.description: The warrior doesn't require air, food, drink, or sleep.

actions.name: Battleaxe
actions.description: Melee Weapon Attack: +6 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit: 8 (1d8 + 4) slashing damage, or 9 (1d10 + 4) slashing damage if used with two hands.

actions.name: Longbow
actions.description: Ranged Weapon Attack: +3 to hit, range 150/600 ft., one target. Hit: 5 (1d8 + 1) piercing damage.

bonus_actions.name: Martial Fury
bonus_actions.description: The warrior makes one Battleaxe or Longbow attack, and attack rolls against it have advantage until the start of its next turn.

features.name: Ambusher
features.description: The serpentmaw has advantage on attack rolls against any creature it has surprised.

features.name: Spider Climb
features.description: The serpentmaw can climb difficult surfaces, including upside down on ceilings, without needing to make an ability check.

actions.name: Multiattack
actions.description: The serpentmaw makes two attacks: one with its bite and one with its tail.

actions.name: Bite
actions.description: Melee Weapon Attack: +7 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit: 15 (2d10+4) piercing damage plus 7 (2d6) poison damage.

actions.name: Tail
actions.description: Melee Weapon Attack: +7 to hit, reach 10 ft., one target. Hit: 11 (2d6+4) bludgeoning damage, and the target must succeed on a DC 14 Strength saving throw or be knocked prone.

monsters.name: Alyxian the Hunter
damage_immunities: bludgeoning, piercing, and slashing from nonmagical attacks that aren't adamantine
languages: understands the languages of its creator but can't speak

features.name: Immutable Form
features.description: The golem is immune to any spell or effect that would alter its form.

features.name: Magic Resistance
features.description: The golem has advantage on saving throws against spells and other magical effects.

features.name: Magic Weapons
features.description: The golem's weapon attacks are magical.

actions.name: Multiattack
actions.description: The golem makes two slam attacks.

actions.name: Slam
actions.description: Melee Weapon Attack: +10 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit: 19 (3d8+6) bludgeoning damage.

actions.name: Slow (Recharge 5-6)
actions.description: The golem targets one or more creatures it can see within 10 ft. of it. Each target must make a DC 17 Wisdom saving throw against this magic. On a failed save, a target can't use reactions, its speed is halved, and it can't make more than one attack on its turn. In addition, the target can take either an action or a bonus action on its turn, not both. These effects last for 1 minute. A target can repeat the saving throw at the end of each of its turns, ending the effect on itself on a success.

actions.name: Ruidium Dart (Action)
actions.description: As an action, the golem can conjure a magic dart made of ruidium and hurl it at another creature it can see within 120 feet of itself. The dart strikes the target unerringly and vanishes on contact. The target must make a DC 17 Charisma saving throw. On a failed saving throw, the target takes 24 (7d6) psychic damage and gains 1 level of exhaustion. In addition, if the target is not already suffering from ruidium corruption, it becomes corrupted when it fails the saving throw. On a successful saving throw, the target takes half as much damage and suffers no other effects.

features.name: Psychic Maelstrom
features.description: Any creature that starts its turn within 15 feet of the shark must succeed on a DC 17 Wisdom saving throw or take 11 (2d10) psychic damage.

features.name: Regeneration
features.description: The shark regains 10 hit points at the start of its turn. If the shark takes radiant damage or suffers a critical hit, this trait doesn't function at the start of its next turn. The shark dies only if it starts its turn with 0 hit points and doesn't regenerate.

features.name: Water Breathing
features.description: The shark can breathe only underwater.

actions.name: Bite
actions.description: Melee Weapon Attack: +10 to hit (with advantage if the target is a creature missing any hit points), reach 5 ft., one target. Hit: 22 (3d10 + 6) piercing damage, and if the target is a creature, it must succeed on a DC 17 Charisma saving throw or gain 1 level of exhaustion.

features.name: Shield Layers
features.description: Each shield layer around the Effigy of Ruidus has its own property: Purple Layer. This layer crackles with magical energy that deals 14 (4d6) lightning damage to any creature that starts its turn within 10 feet of the Effigy of Ruidus. Maroon Layer. This layer releases a pulse of necrotic energy every time the Effigy of Ruidus takes damage. The pulse deals 7 (2d6) necrotic damage to creatures in the chamber. Vermilion Layer. This layer increases the moon's AC from 17 to 22.

actions.name: Mind Warp
actions.description: Melee or Ranged Spell Attack: +9 to hit, reach 5 ft. or range 120 ft., one creature. Hit: 14 (4d6) psychic damage.

monsters.name: Alyxian the Tormented

features.name: Apotheonic Rejuvenation
features.description: When Alyxian drops to O hit points, his body dies and cracks open like a cocoon. Alyxian instantly emerges from the cocoon in his second form, Alyxian the Callous, in the space where his previous form died. His initiative count doesn't change.

features.name: Divinely Blessed
features.description: Alyxian can't be surprised and can't be changed into another form against his will.

features.name: Legendary Resistance (2/Day)
features.description: If Alyxian fails a saving throw, he can choose to succeed instead.

actions.name: Multiattack
actions.description: Alyxian makes two Grasping Hand attacks.

actions.name: Grasping Hand

Each creature in a 10-foot-radius sphere centered on the exploding bloodfin, including any creature swallowed by the bloodfin, must succeed on a DC 15 Constitution saving throw or take 10 (3d6) poison damage. A creature inside the bloodfin when it explodes falls prone in the space formerly occupied by the bloodfin and is no longer blinded or restrained by it.

features.name: Water Breathing
features.description: The bloodfin can breathe only underwater.

actions.name: Multiattack
actions.description: The bloodfin makes one Bite attack and one Tail attack.

actions.name: Bite
actions.description: Melee Weapon Attack: +9 to hit (with advantage if the target is a creature missing any hit points), reach 5 ft., one target. Hit: 14 (2d8 + 5) piercing damage, and if the target is a creature, it is grappled (escape DC 15). Until this grapple ends, the target is restrained, and the bloodfin can't bite another target.

actions.name: Tail
actions.description: Melee Weapon Attack: +9 to hit (with advantage if the target is a creature missing any hit points), reach 10 ft., one target. Hit: 19 (4d6 + 5) bludgeoning damage.

monsters.name: Swarm of Sorrowfish
monsters.senses: blindsight 60 ft. (blind beyond this radius), passive Perception 10

features.name: Swarm
features.description: The swarm can occupy another creature's space and vice versa, and the swarm can move through an opening as narrow as 1 foot wide. The swarm can't regain hit points or gain temporary hit points.

features.name: Virulent Sorrow
features.description: Each time the swarm takes damage, any creature within 5 feet of it must make a DC 13 Wisdom saving throw. On a failed saving throw, the creature suffers the following effects until the end of its next turn: it has disadvantage on its attack rolls, it can't take reactions, and its speed is halved.

features.name: Water Breathing
features.description: The swarm can breathe only underwater.

actions.name: Swarm of Bites
actions.description: Melee Weapon Attack: +8 to hit, reach 0 ft., one target in the swarm's space. Hit: 21 (6d6) piercing damage, or 10 (3d6) piercing damage if the swarm has half its hit points or fewer.

actions.name: Desolate Drain (Recharge 5-6)
actions.description: Each creature in the swarm's space must make a DC 13 Wisdom saving throw. On a failed saving throw, a creature takes 24 (7d6) psychic damage and is stunned until the end of its next turn. The effect ends on a creature if the swarm moves out of the creature's space or if another creature within 5 feet of the swarm uses an action to make a DC 14 Strength check, pulling the affected creature out of the swarm on a successful check. On a successful saving throw, a creature takes half as much damage and suffers no other effects.

monsters.name: Sword Wraith Commander
damage_resistances: bludgeoning, piercing, and slashing from nonmagical attacks
languages: the languages it knew in life

features.name: Turning Defiance
features.description: The commander and any other sword wraiths within 30 feet of it have advantage on saving throws against effects that turn Undead.

features.name: Unusual Nature
features.description: The commander doesn't require air, food, drink, or sleep.

actions.name: Multiattack
actions.description: The commander makes two Longsword or Longbow attacks.

actions.name: Longsword
actions.description: Melee Weapon Attack: +7 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit: 8 (1d8 + 4) slashing damage, or 9 (1d10 + 4) slashing damage if used with two hands.

actions.name: Longbow
actions.description: Ranged Weapon Attack: +5 to hit, range 150/600 ft., one target. Hit: 6 (1d8 + 2) piercing damage.

actions.name: Call to Honor (1/Day)
actions.description: If the commander has taken damage during this combat, it gives itself advantage on attack rolls until the end of its next turn, and 1d4 + 1 sword wraith warriors appear in unoccupied spaces within 30 feet of it. The warriors last until they drop to 0 hit points, and they take their turns immediately after the commander's turn on the same initiative count.

bonus_actions.name: Martial Fury
bonus_actions.description: The commander makes one Longsword or Longbow attack, which deals an extra 9 (2d8) necrotic damage on a hit, and attack rolls against it have advantage until the start of its next turn.

npcs.name: Ayo Jabe
npcs.description: As the de facto leader of a new, unnamed adventuring party, Ayo Jabe has a lot of responsibility on her shoulders. She and her companions have worked odd jobs around the town of Jigow for a few weeks now, and she's starting to feel confident that they're ready for real adventure. Ayo is a water genasi who was born to ore parents during a terrible storm in the Emerald Gulch. Her family has lived injigow for generations, and she's eager to leave home and see the world. Ayo picked up her combat skills while working as a hunter for the town of Jigow. She recently joined up with her childhood friend Dermot, as well as Maggie Keeneyes, a mercenary who came to town several weeks ago. Despite Maggie's brusque demeanor, she became a loyal friend of Ayo and Dermot, and the three of them have become inseparable, even as more adventurers have joined their party. Ayo is hotheaded and appreciates people who make decisions as impulsively as she does. Nevertheless, she respects Dermot's even-tempered advice and dutifully plays the role of the wise leader. She has no patience for people who are indecisive, and she is infuriated by people who don't say what they really mean.

npcs.name: Dermot Wurder
npcs.description: When you're the twelfth son of a poor goblin family inJigow, the only way to make a name for yourself is to become a great champion- someone who can win bragging contests in the local taverns night after night. Young Dermot Wurder, however, wasn't interested in performing feats of strength or agility that would win him a boast-worthy epithet. Fame wasn't for him, nor was the aggressiveness that becoming famous required. He was more interested in cooking, planting flowers, and sewing clothes- doing the work that kept his family together while his carefree siblings dove off waterfalls and wrestled stray dogs. Dermot and Ayo Jabe have known each other long enough that their first meeting has vanished into the haze of youthful pre-memory. Dermot accompanied Ayo whenever he could, packing herbs and medicines when they went exploring in the woods. When Ayo recently told him of her dream to form an adventuring party, he started training to wear heavy armor and threw himself into studying the faith of the Luxon so he could wield the blessings of the light to protect those he cares about. Dermot is fiercely protective of his friends and furiously rebukes anyone who disparages or threatens them. His deepest need- one even he doesn't know he has- is to make a friend who will help him realize what he wants for himself.

npcs.name: Galsariad Ardyth
npcs.description: Beautiful, ethereal, deathly, shadowy- all accurately describe Galsariad Ardyth, a drow in his two-hundredth year of life. He's recently taken up the study of arcane magic, and he's pursuing the life of an adventurer in hopes of improving his reputation within the Kryn Dynasty. Loquacious, snarky, and sarcastic to a fault, he's ready with a barb for any occasion- usually to mask his own insecurities. A city-dweller from the Kryn capital of Rosohna, Galsariad is blessed with sharp aesthetic sensibilities and an interest in ancient lore, especially history concerning the Age of Arcanum, Exandria's long-lost magical golden age. He's also the newest member of the rival party, and both Ayo and Irvan are impressed by his ethereal elegance- and have a bit of a crush on him, even if he does talk too much. Galsariad appreciates people who share his interests and are willing to spend time studying with him, though he also likes it when people treat him with respect even if they don't care about magic. He dislikes people who keep secrets from him, and hates when people judge him for being a novice at magic even though he's centuries old.

npcs.name: Durth Mirimm
npcs.description: A drow political liaison for the Kryn Dynasty in Jigow, serving as an intermediary between Jigow's elders and the court of the Bright Queen Leylas Kryn.

npcs.name: Irvan Wastewalker
npcs.description: A young male human participant in the pie-eating contest at the Festival of Merit. His stat block appears in appendix A (tier 1).
npcs.source: Chapter 1 - A Fateful Competition, area J1

npcs.name: Maryl Bronzefang
npcs.description: The victor in this contest, and the defending champion of the event, is Maryl Bronzefang, a lawful neutral, ore gladiator. A native of Jigow serving in Bazzoxan's Aurora Watch, she was given leave to return home for the festival.

npcs.name: Maggie Keeneyes
npcs.description: After prodding Dermot to try the maze in area J2, Maggie Keeneyes can be found here, eager to compete.

npcs.name: Vars
npcs.description: A quiet male goblin commoner — Vars, the owner of the butcher shop — sits off to the side, managing the wagers made by onlookers.

npcs.name: Beetle
npcs.description: This event is managed by two neutral good goblins named Beetle and Zag. Their farm is jointly run by the Gakthash and Uvuroh goblin clans, and every year, the goblin couple uses the festival competitions as a labor-saving way to harvest their crops.

npcs.name: Zag
npcs.description: This event is managed by two neutral good goblins named Beetle and Zag. Their farm is jointly run by the Gakthash and Uvuroh goblin clans, and every year, the goblin couple uses the festival competitions as a labor-saving way to harvest their crops.

npcs.name: Irvan
npcs.description: After the pie-eating contest in area J1, Irvan can also be found relaxing here. If a character needs a partner, Irvan grudgingly volunteers to be their teammate for the event.

npcs.name: Elder Colbu Kaz
npcs.description: A chaotic neutral, goblin priest who created three puzzles for a contest.

npcs.name: Justice
npcs.description: and his moorbounder mount, Rice Pudding, are here if they survived the Moorbounder Mayhem encounter. If the characters helped him during that encounter, Justice gives them a pair of goggles of night that the caravan he's working for had a hard time selling at their last stop.

npcs.name: Postraeck (Six-Knives)
npcs.description: A grizzled man named Postraeck, a neutral evil bandit captain who rides an imposing black warhorse. Better known as Six-Knives because of the six daggers he carries on his person at all times, each of which has a name (Boneshaver, Gleam, Grudge, Jabby, Pierce, and Tickles).

npcs.name: Pops Kelbadurn
npcs.description: served in the Asarius Town Guard and still has his old chain mail, spear, and shield stored in the command post (area L2f). He's easygoing and artistic.

npcs.name: Auntie jailer
npcs.description: old and elegant-looking, thanks to her long silver hair and deep green robes. She calls herself an "old witch" and spends much of her time brewing potions and inventing new tea blends.

npcs.name: Little Gothby
npcs.description: a dutiful 5-year-old. He doesn't talk to strangers but instead heads for one of his dads if he is approached.

npcs.name: Little Chespa
npcs.description: 3 years old. She can speak in full sentences, and can read and write as well as an adult. She likes to hop down off the tortoise and frolic through the clearing.

npcs.name: Gaeya Iliera
npcs.description: cooking some of the best mastodon kor'rundl to be found outside of Asarius. This savory dish is a hearty rice bowl topped with spicy grilled mastodon and smoky-flavored kor'run, a vegetable like a deep red squash grown in Rosohna's sunless gardens. A character who partakes of this food awakens the next morning with 1d10 temporary hit points that last for the next 24 hours.

npcs.name: Tyvak
npcs.description: survived the battle with the udaak that the characters saw the aftermath of in the Demonic Carrion encounter. She is the daughter of Kierchaly Wastewalker and belongs to the same clan as Irvan Wastewalker. If Tyvak sees that one of the characters has retrieved her father's +1 dagger from that site, she offers to trade her +1 battleaxe for it and thanks the characters with all her heart if the dagger is turned over.

npcs.name: Moghra
npcs.description: survived the battle with the udaak that the characters saw the aftermath of in the Demonic Carrion encounter. He is the son of Kierchaly Wastewalker and belongs to the same clan as Irvan Wastewalker.

npcs.name: Lanata
npcs.description: One of the Acorn Sisters, dryads. As the caretakers of this forest, they're fine with bonfires as long as only dead wood is burned. It's customary to share food, drink, and song with them in appreciation for their hospitality. Characters who show them great respect by making an offering directly to them awaken in the morning with a charm of vitality (see the rules for supernatural gifts in the Dungeon Master's Guide).

npcs.name: Robur
npcs.description: One of the Acorn Sisters, dryads. As the caretakers of this forest, they're fine with bonfires as long as only dead wood is burned. It's customary to share food, drink, and song with them in appreciation for their hospitality. Characters who show them great respect by making an offering directly to them awaken in the morning with a charm of vitality (see the rules for supernatural gifts in the Dungeon Master's Guide).

npcs.name: Verin

features.name: Fey Ancestry
features.description: Verin has advantage on saving throws against being charmed, and magic can't put him to sleep.

features.name: Sunlight Sensitivity
features.description: While in sunlight, Verin has disadvantage on attack rolls, as well as on Wisdom (Perception) checks that rely on sight.

features.name: Manifest Echo
features.description: Verin magically creates an echo—a translucent, gray object that looks like him. The echo appears in an unoccupied space Verin can see within 15 feet of himself. While the echo exists, Verin chooses whether each of his attacks originates from his space or the echo's space. On Verin's turn, the echo can move in accordance with Verin's wishes. The echo has AC 17 and 1 hit point. It otherwise uses Verin's statistics. The echo lasts for 1 minute or until it is destroyed, until Verin ends his turn more than 30 feet away from it, until Verin manifests another echo, or until Verin is incapacitated.

features.name: Reposition
features.description: Verin magically swaps places with his echo.

actions.name: Multiattack
actions.description: Verin makes three Glaive attacks.

actions.name: Glaive
actions.description: Melee Weapon Attack: +7 to hit, reach 10 ft., one target. Hit: 9 (1d10 + 4) slashing damage.

actions.name: Hand Crossbow
actions.description: Ranged Weapon Attack: +7 to hit, range 30/120 ft., one target. Hit: 5 (1d6 + 2) piercing damage plus 22 (4d10) poison damage.

actions.name: Spellcasting
actions.description: Verin casts one of the following spells, requiring no material components and using Charisma as the spellcasting ability (spell save DC 14): At will: dancing lights. 1/day each: darkness, faerie fire, levitate (self only).

npcs.description: Verin is the leader of Bazzoxan, a drow elf of lawful good alignment, who commands the Aurora Watch and defends the town.

npcs.name: Reynard Allerton
npcs.description: A willowy man wearing a leather apron, a chaotic good scout.

npcs.name: Sebastian Allerton
npcs.description: A giant of a man: muscular, blue-eyed, with short-cropped hair and a missing arm, a neutral good thug.

npcs.name: Prolix Yusaf
npcs.description: A bookish tiefling, a scholarly agent from the Allegiance of Allsight.

npcs.name: Bautha Dyrr
npcs.description: A lawful neutral drow priest who disapproves of the reclamation efforts in Bazzoxan, but strives to heal and protect those in need.

npcs.name: Naevyn Tasithar
npcs.description: A neutral good scout. She weakly salutes the characters, then asks them to hand her her satchel. She pulls out a small tiger's eye carving of a rabbit with her name carved into the bottom. Naevyn explains that she was planning to visit the Wall of the Unforgotten (area B6) and place this trinket there.

npcs.name: Kalym
npcs.description: A priest stationed at the wall (area B6). Characters who speak to Kalym can learn Naevyn's reason.

npcs.name: Taskhand Verin Thelyss
npcs.description: Taskhand Verin Thelyss and his senior officers. Verin greets the characters with warmth and gentle concern. He shares information about Bazzoxan and the Betrayers' Rise.

npcs.name: Aloysia
npcs.description: An agent of a foreign organization calling itself the Consortium of the Vermilion Dream. An elf named Aloysia has been reprimanded for trying to bribe Aurora Watch soldiers to protect her while she searches for an ancient holy site she claims is within the Betrayers' Rise.

npcs.name: Prolix
npcs.description: An archaeologist from the Allegiance of Allsight in Ank'Harel. He is ostensibly assisting Aurora Watch arcanists who are researching ways to seal the rift within the Betrayers' Rise. Verin suspects that the archaeologist has other motives, because he was seen earlier in the day lurking around the crematorium (area B2).

npcs.description: One member of the Cobalt Soul expedition, a tiefling named Question, went with his group up to the gate of the Betrayers' Rise but elected not to enter the place. He's holed up at the Ready Room (area B7), ready to talk about his research with anyone who will listen.

npcs.name: Foghome
npcs.description: A neutral good, firbolg priest named Foghome moves through the temple at all hours of the day. He is a follower of Melora the Wild Mother, but he recognizes the temple as a former holy place of Avandra the Change Bringer. He hopes to honor both deities by cultivating new life in the midst of the death and destruction that haunts this place.

npcs.name: Kalym Telaarin
npcs.description: A drow priest of the Luxon, 300 years old, with many scars on his otherwise handsome face. His left leg from the knee down is an intricate prosthetic carved from chitinous black rock and ringed with bands of pale purple light.

npcs.name: Delez Demona
npcs.description: Runs the bar and the kitchen and handles most interactions with customers.

npcs.name: Prima Demona
npcs.description: Manages the finances and inventory.

npcs.name: Aloysia Telfan
npcs.description: Aloysia Telfan, a lawful evil, elf occult initiate (see appendix A) who thirsts for knowledge and power.

npcs.name: Bas Lyrean

npcs.name: Kovra Lyrean
npcs.description: Twin sister who runs Lyrean Linen, a front for a black market selling suude and other forbidden concoctions.

npcs.name: Irawan

npcs.name: Calinao

npcs.name: Iwo Zalarre
npcs.description: Sardonic monk who oversees visitors to the public archives of the Temple of the Mentor.

npcs.name: Watcher Byron
npcs.description: Oversees most of the Sentinels of Memory's operations for Watcher Trast, rarely leaves the Tower of Memory.

npcs.name: Lymmle Wist

npcs.source: Chapter 4 | The Jewel of Hope p.101

npcs.source: Chapter 4 | The Jewel of Hope p.101

npcs.name: Shira

features.description:
Shira casts one of the following spells, requiring no material components and using Charisma as the spellcasting ability (spell save DC 10, +2 to hit with spell attacks):
At will: chill touch
1/day each: blindness/deafness, ray of sickness

npcs.source: Chapter 4 | The Jewel of Hope p.105

npcs.name: Ena
npcs.description: Ena (neutral, human berserker) masquerades as a casino patron.

npcs.name: Duskwood
npcs.description: Duskwood (chaotic neutral, half-elf spy), like Ena, masquerades as a casino patron and wears a hat of disguise.

npcs.name: Koris

npcs.description: Koris (lawful neutral, tiefling assassin), the crew's leader, works at one of the casino's card tables- a job she has held for about a month. She carries a potion of gaseous form, a tiny packet containing dust of disappearance, and a bag of holding.

npcs.name: Relickeeper Kareema

features.description: The agent has advantage on Intelligence (Arcana, History, Investigation, Nature, or Religion) checks.

actions.name: Dagger
actions.description: Melee or Ranged Weapon Attack: +2 to hit, reach 5 ft. or range 20/60 ft., one target. Hit: 2 (1d4) piercing damage.

npcs.description: A neutral good, ore scholarly agent with messy dark curls and round glasses.

It has the following wizard spells prepared: Cantrips (at will): mage hand, prestidigitation, ray of frost; 1st level (4 slots): detect magic, disguise self, shield, sleep; 2nd level (3 slots): invisibility, suggestion; 3rd level (2 slots): counterspell, fireball.

actions.name: Dagger
actions.description: Melee or Ranged Weapon Attack: +4 to hit, reach 5 ft. or range 20/60 ft., one target. Hit: 4 (1d4+2) piercing damage.

npcs.description: A lawful neutral, elf scholarly mastermind.

npcs.name: Scholarly Excavator

features.name: Diligent
features.description: The excavator has advantage on Strength (Athletics) checks made to climb, dig, or lift.

actions.name: Pickaxe
actions.description: Melee Weapon Attack: +4 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit: 6 (1d8+2) piercing damage.

actions.name: Light Crossbow
actions.description: Ranged Weapon Attack: +3 to hit, range 80/320 ft., one target. Hit: 5 (1d8+1) piercing damage.

npcs.description: A lawful neutral scholarly excavator serving as a bodyguard.

npcs.name: Laurin Ophidas

features.name: Immunity to poison damage and poisoned condition
features.description: He has immunity to poison damage and the poisoned condition.

features.name: Staff of the Adder attunement
features.description: He wields a staff of the adder and is attuned to it as though he were a cleric.

npcs.description: A chaotic evil half-elf cultist of Zehir, using the cult fanatic stat block with modifications.

npcs.name: Jamil A'alithiya

npcs.description: A neutral evil, dwarf occult silvertongue who's one of the masters of the Consortium of the Vermilion Dream.

npcs.name: Satzrak Runestrider
npcs.description: A neutral evil, blue dragonborn occult extollant (see appendix A for both stat blocks), are in First Eclipse's taproom.

features.name: Resistance
features.description: She has resistance to fire damage

features.name: Darkvision
features.description: darkvision out to a range of 60 feet

features.description: The professor speaks Aquan, Common, Infernal, and Ore.

features.description: Scribble understands Auran and Common but speaks only through mimicry. He can imitate any sounds he has heard, including voices.

npcs.description: Scribble uses the scholarly agent stat block (see appendix A), with this change: Scribble understands Auran and Common but speaks only through mimicry. He can imitate any sounds he has heard, including voices.

npcs.name: Xot

features.description: Xot speaks Common and Giant.

features.name: Cold Resistance
features.description: She has resistance to cold damage

features.description: counts as one size larger when determining her carrying capacity and the weight she can push, drag, or lift.

npcs.name: Olara

features.name: Swimming Speed
features.description: She has a swimming speed equal to her walking speed, and she can breathe air and water.

features.name: Darkvision
features.description: She has darkvision out to a range of 60 feet.

features.name: Cold Resistance and Charm Advantage
features.description: She has resistance to cold damage and advantage on saving throws to end the charmed condition on herself. Magic can't put her to sleep.

features.name: Ancient Dialect
features.description: Olara speaks an ancient dialect that formed the basis for both Elvish and Ore, and any character who speaks and understands either of those languages can converse with her.

npcs.description: A neutral good sea elf named Olara floats behind a granite countertop in the Sunken Tavern (M6). She is one of the few mortals who survived Gruumsh's attack centuries ago, subsisting on kelp. Decades spent near the Netherdeep and the Alyxian Aboleth have damaged her memories.

npcs.name: Galeokaerda

features.name: Modifications to stat block
features.description: Modify Galeokaerda's stat block as follows: • Galeokaerda speaks Celestial, Common, and Elvish. • She has darkvision out to a range of 60 feet. • She has advantage on saving throws against being charmed, and magic can't put her to sleep.

npcs.description: A neutral evil, high elf occult extollant (see appendix A) named Galeokaerda has set up camp in this room along with Crescent, her shield guardian. Galeokaerda wears the shield guardian's amulet around her neck but hides it under her shirt.

npcs.name: Talmyth
npcs.description: A veteran covered in blood limps toward the characters and says, "You won the day, brave Alyxian. My wounds burn, but if you command it, I will follow you to the end."

npcs.name: Theo Nathope

features.name: Incorporeal Movement
features.description: Theo can pass through solid objects and end his turn inside one.

features.name: Truesight
features.description: Theo has truesight out to a range of 60 feet.

features.name: Cannot be harmed, banished, or dispelled
features.description: This apparition can't be harmed, banished, or dispelled.

npcs.description: A ghostly boy bearing a striking resemblance to Alyxian as a young boy. He guides characters through the Netherdeep.

npcs.name: Perigee the Deva
npcs.description: The blue-skinned angel is a deva named Perigee. She is a servant of the Moon Weaver who fought with Alyxian in his final battle. Perigee was destroyed but later re-formed at the Moon Weaver's side. For centuries thereafter, she searched for Alyxian and eventually found her way to the Netherdeep, where she became mired in despair and corrupted by ruidium.

traps.trigger: A creature tries to swim past the ghostgrass

detection.detail: The pale plants blocking the exit to the cavern are ghostgrass, a carnivorous variety of sea grass.

disarm.detail: A creature can use an action to try to free itself or another creature within its reach from the ghostgrass, doing so with a successful DC 12 Strength (Athletics) check.

traps.effect: A creature that tries to swim past the ghostgrass must succeed on a DC 12 Dexterity saving throw or take 3 (1d6) necrotic damage and be restrained. A restrained creature takes the damage again at the start of each of its turns until it escapes.
traps.area: A thick patch of bone-white sea grass blocking the exit to the cavern
traps.description: A carnivorous variety of sea grass that restrains and damages creatures that fail a Dexterity save.

traps.name: Landslide
traps.trigger: As you swim into this area, ripples course through the water as more rocky debris begins to slide toward you.

detection.detail: One side of the chamber is covered in the crumbled and muddy remains of a landslide.

traps.effect: Each character must make a DC 14 Dexterity saving throw, taking 10 (3d6) bludgeoning damage from the landslide on a failed save, or half as much damage on a successful one.
traps.area: One side of the chamber covered in crumbled and muddy remains of a landslide
traps.description: A landslide of rocky debris that damages characters who fail a Dexterity save.

traps.name: Sacrifice Engine
traps.trigger: A creature is in the pit while the blades are spinning

detection.detail: The pit is 30 feet deep and lined with rows of silver blades; a lever near the edge can be pulled to spin the blades.

disarm.detail: Pulling the lever near the edge of the pit stops the blades from spinning.

traps.effect: A creature in the pit while the blades are spinning takes 44 (8d10) slashing damage at the start of each of its turns.
traps.description: A 30-foot-deep pit lined with rows of silver blades that can be made to spin by pulling a lever near the edge.

traps.name: Vrock Corpse Spore Eruption
traps.trigger: A failed DC 15 Wisdom (Survival) check to extract the contents of the vrock's stomach.

detection.detail: To extract the contents of the vrock's stomach, a character must first cleave through the vrock's hide.

disarm.detail: No disarm method described; avoid triggering by succeeding on the Survival check.

traps.effect: An eruption of spores from the vrock's corpse that fill a 10-foot-radius sphere centered on the corpse. All creatures in that area must succeed on a DC 14 Constitution saving throw or become poisoned. A creature poisoned in this way takes 5 (1d10) poison damage at the start of each of its turns. It can repeat the saving throw at the end of each of its turns, ending the effect on itself on a success.
traps.description: A failed attempt to cut open a dead vrock's stomach causes a spore eruption.

traps.name: Bladed Corridor
traps.trigger: Whenever one or more creatures are in the hall, the floor tilts to one side and then the other so that creatures stumble into the blades.

detection.detail: Characters who have a passive Wisdom (Perception) score of 12 or higher notice a phrase written in Undercommon on the floor between the two statues.

disarm.detail: If the crystal canister is destroyed, the characters have no way to disable the hall's trap.

traps.effect: A creature that moves into the corridor or starts its turn there must make a DC 20 Dexterity saving throw, taking 17 (5d6) slashing damage on a failed saving throw, or half as much damage on a successful one.
traps.area: The corridor north of the statues
traps.description: A corridor with twitching silver blades protruding from its walls; the floor tilts to make creatures stumble into the blades.

traps.name: Stained-Glass Mosaic Trap
traps.trigger: A creature presses an incorrect symbol on the mosaic

detection.detail: A character who succeeds on a DC 11 Intelligence (Religion) check recognizes these as the symbols of evil gods.

disarm.method: Pressing the correct four symbols in order
disarm.detail: If four of the symbols are pressed in the correct order, as noted in the Symbol Sequence table, a door opens at the base of the wall.

traps.effect: A creature that presses an incorrect symbol must make a DC 16 Wisdom saving throw, taking 28 (8d6) psychic damage on a failed save, or half as much damage on a successful one.
traps.description: A 10-foot-wide section of wall at the north end of the basilica resembles a tall, stained-glass window. Its imagery changes constantly, but nine symbols remain static. If four of the symbols are pressed in the correct order, a door opens. Pressing an incorrect symbol deals psychic damage.

traps.name: Chains of Darkness Trap
traps.trigger: A creature falls prone in the hall (area R10)

detection.detail: A creature that enters this hall immediately feels weighed down and senses a terrible dread. The creature must make a DC 14 Wisdom saving throw.

disarm.detail: Any creature that is not grappled by the chains can use an action to try to free a chained creature within reach, doing so with a successful DC 15 Strength (Athletics) check.

traps.effect: The creature must succeed on a DC 15 Dexterity saving throw or be grappled by the chains (escape DC 15). Until it escapes, the creature takes 5 (1d10) psychic damage at the start of each of its turns. Whatever the result of the check, the creature making the attempt takes 11 (2d10) psychic damage.
traps.damage: 5 (1d10) per turn while grappled; 11 (2d10) to the rescuer
traps.description: When a creature falls prone in this hall, the chains on the floor slither toward it, and the figures carved in the walls drone in low voices. The creature must succeed on a DC 15 Dexterity saving throw or be grappled by the chains, taking psychic damage each turn.

traps.name: Abyssal Rift
traps.trigger: When a creature passes through the gaping mouth of the stone-carved face of Gruumsh in area R15

detection.detail: The rift is visible as a 10-foot-wide, 20-foot-long orifice filled with impenetrable darkness. Horrible shrieks emanate from it.

disarm.detail: The rift closes after 1 minute automatically. No disarm method is given.

traps.effect: A creature that enters the rift from this side is magically transported, along with anything it is wearing or carrying, to the Abyss. The creature emerges from a similar rift located inside a colossal cyclone of poisonous gas. A creature caught in the cyclone is trapped there and takes 14 (4d6) poison damage at the start of each of its turns. A creature that has a flying speed can escape the cyclone by flying into the rift; a creature without a flying speed can use an action to try to harness the winds of the cyclone, propelling itself through the rift with a successful DC 19 Dexterity (Acrobatics) check.
traps.description: A planar rift that opens in the floor on the east side of the chasm when a creature passes through the carving of Gruumsh's face. It is a gateway to the Abyss.

traps.name: Vault Trap
traps.trigger: If the vault is opened by any means other than using the master key, the vault's magical trap is triggered.

detection.detail: A character who examines the vault and succeeds on a successful DC 20 Intelligence (Investigation) check finds a thin keyhole near its base.

disarm.detail: The trap can't be disarmed, but successfully casting dispel magic (DC 15) on the lock before an attempt is made to open it suppresses the trap for 1 minute, allowing the lock to be manipulated without negative consequences.

traps.effect: Each creature within 5 feet of the vault must make a DC 16 Wisdom saving throw. On a failed saving throw, a creature takes 36 (8d8) psychic damage and is stunned for 1 minute. On a successful save, a creature takes half as much damage and isn't stunned.
traps.area: Each creature within 5 feet of the vault
traps.description: A magical trap on the casino's coin vault that triggers if opened without the master key.

traps.name: Vault Door Energy Blast Trap
traps.trigger: Forcing the vault door open (DC 21 Strength (Athletics) check)

detection.detail: A character who searches the basement and succeeds on a DC 15 Wisdom (Perception) check notices the faint outline of a circular stone door in the wall next to a bookcase that is bolted to the floor.

traps.effect: A loud, concussive blast of energy fills a 15-foot cube immediately outside the vault. Any creature in the cube must make a DC 18 Constitution saving throw, taking 33 (6d10) thunder damage on a failed save, or half as much damage on a successful one.
traps.description: A magical trap that releases a concussive blast of energy when the vault door is forced open.

traps.name: Trapdoor (disguised as symbol of Corellon)
traps.trigger: A character who searches the tower ruins and succeeds on a DC 15 Intelligence (Investigation) check discovers a large symbol of Corellon inscribed on the floor, mostly hidden under sand and debris. Closer examination discloses a 5-foot-diameter, circular stone trapdoor disguised as part of the symbol.

detection.detail: A character who searches the tower ruins and succeeds on a DC 15 Intelligence (Investigation) check discovers a large symbol of Corellon inscribed on the floor, mostly hidden under sand and debris. Closer examination discloses a 5-foot-diameter, circular stone trapdoor disguised as part of the symbol.

disarm.detail: The trapdoor is closed and stuck. A character can use an action to try to pry it up by using a crowbar or similar tool.

traps.effect: The trapdoor is closed and stuck. A character can use an action to try to pry it up by using a crowbar or similar tool.
traps.description: A stone trapdoor disguised as part of a symbol of Corellon, stuck and requiring effort to open.

traps.name: Burst of Radiance Trap
traps.trigger: A creature enters the armory without first saying a prayer to Corellon.

detection.detail: A character who searches the opening for traps and succeeds on a DC 17 Intelligence (Investigation) check spots a tiny glyph inscribed along the edge of the opening, in a location that's not visible while the trapdoor is closed.

disarm.method: dispel magic (DC 17) or defaced using mason's tools or similar equipment
disarm.detail: If this glyph is dispelled with a successful casting of dispel magic (DC 17) or defaced using mason's tools or similar equipment, the following trap ceases to function.

traps.effect: A burst of radiance flares from the chamber. Each creature in the armory and within 15 feet of the trapdoor must make a DC 18 Constitution saving throw, taking 33 (6d10) radiant damage on a failed save, or half as much damage on a successful one. This trap can be triggered only once.
traps.area: The armory and within 15 feet of the trapdoor
traps.description: A magical trap that triggers a burst of radiant damage when a creature enters the armory without praying to Corellon.

traps.name: Secret Door (Netherdeep)
traps.trigger: Any creature within 10 feet of a secret door that deals damage to it

detection.detail: A character who spends at least 10 minutes searching an area for secret doors can make a DC 20 Intelligence (Investigation) check at the end of that search. If the check succeeds and there's a secret door to be found, the character finds it.

disarm.detail: Secret doors in the Netherdeep are unlocked unless otherwise noted, and they open easily despite their great weight.

traps.effect: Any creature within 10 feet of a secret door that deals damage to it must make a DC 15 Constitution saving throw, taking 22 (4d10) psychic damage on a failed save, or half as much damage on a successful one.
traps.description: A secret door made of ruidium-veined stone that deals psychic damage to creatures that damage it.

traps.name: Boiling Water (Vents of Fury)
traps.trigger: If the bloodfin is killed, the vents in the floor flare with bright red light and spew forth a flood of boiling-hot water.

detection.detail: Characters who have a passive Wisdom (Perception) score of 17 or higher notice something more: At the far end of the thirty-foot-high cavern, a monstrous fish with a red-streaked body chases a school of much smaller fish.

traps.effect: Any creature that starts its turn in the boiling-hot water must make a DC 15 Constitution saving throw, taking 21 (6d6) fire damage on a failed saving throw, or half as much damage on a successful one. The scalding heat lasts for 1 hour, after which the vents return to their normal illumination and the water temperature in the cavern again becomes bearably warm.
traps.description: The bubbling columns of water rising from the vents are hot, but not hot enough to damage creatures that enter them. If the bloodfin is killed, the vents spew boiling-hot water.

traps.name: Ruidium Spines (Current Trap)
traps.trigger: If the characters kill the light devourer, the current intensifies for 1 hour. Until the current returns to normal, any creature that starts its turn in this chamber must succeed on a DC 14 Strength saving throw or be thrust against a wall by the current and skewered by ruidium spines.

detection.detail: The walls are lined with ruidium spines, visible to any creature entering the chamber.

disarm.detail: No disarm method described; the trap is triggered by killing the light devourer.

traps.effect: The creature takes 5 (1d10) piercing damage from the spines and must succeed on a DC 20 Charisma saving throw or gain 1 level of exhaustion. If the creature is not already suffering from ruidium corruption, it becomes corrupted when it fails the saving throw.
traps.description: A current threatens to pull creatures into this chamber, the walls of which are lined with ruidium spines. The Apotheon's ragged breathing is audible. Thermal vents in the floor give off swirling bubbles, dim light, and warmth.

traps.name: Scalding Pit (Boiling Water)
traps.trigger: If either the ruidium greatsword or the ruidium shield is removed from its resting place, the vents in the floor flare with bright red light and spew forth a flood of boiling-hot water

detection.detail: The vents in the floor are visible, but the trap is triggered by removing the items.

disarm.detail: The trap cannot be disarmed; it lasts for 1 hour after triggering.

traps.effect: Any creature that starts its turn in the boiling water must make a DC 15 Constitution saving throw, taking 21 (6d6) fire damage on a failed save, or half as much damage on a successful one. The scalding heat lasts for 1 hour, after which the vents return to their normal illumination and the water temperature changes from boiling hot to bearably warm.
traps.area: The water in the chamber up to a height of 30 feet
traps.description: Natural vents spew red light and jets of bubbling water. Removing the ruidium items triggers a flood of boiling-hot water.

traps.name: Ruidium Tendrils (Apotheon's Fury)
traps.trigger: When all three serpentmaws in area N13 are dead, dozens of tendrils of ruidium emerge from the statues in the cavern.

detection.detail: The tendrils emerge automatically after the serpentmaws are killed.

disarm.detail: The tendrils persist for 1 minute, after which they recede back into the statues.

traps.effect: Any creature that enters the cavern or starts its turn there must succeed on a DC 15 Dexterity saving throw or be grappled by a tendril (escape DC 15). While grappled in this way, a creature is also restrained. No more than one tendril can grapple a single creature. Each tendril is an Ooze that has AC 15; 10 hit points; immunity to all damage except slashing; Strength, Dexterity, and Constitution scores of 20; and Intelligence, Wisdom, and Charisma scores of 1. A tendril reduced to 0 hit points disintegrates in a crimson haze. On initiative count 0, each creature grappled by a tendril takes 3 (1d6) piercing damage and 3 (1d6) psychic damage as it is flung against one of the cavern's ruidium spikes. The creature remains grappled after taking this damage; in addition, it must succeed on a DC 20 Charisma saving throw or gain 1 level of exhaustion. If the creature is not already suffering from ruidium corruption, it becomes corrupted when it fails the saving throw.
traps.description: When the serpentmaws are killed, ruidium tendrils emerge from statues, grappling and flinging creatures against spikes.

traps.name: East Door Trap
traps.trigger: The first time the door is touched

detection.detail: The door gives off a flash of crimson light when touched.

disarm.detail: A character can use an action to try to pick the lock with thieves' tools, doing so with a successful DC 22 Dexterity check. A knock spell or similar magic also opens the door.

traps.effect: Any creature within 10 feet of the door when this happens must succeed on a DC 18 Strength saving throw or be pushed 20 feet away from the door- and into the death embrace's tentacles, if that creature is still alive and present.
traps.description: A sturdy cellar door with a built-in lock that triggers a crimson flash and pushes creatures away when first touched.
